THIS IS THE SECOND INSTANCE TODAY AND THE OTHER ONE WAS CAREFUL. campaign/the-deed re-derived 0160 against origin/main AFTER main had moved twice, which is better practice than most, and still landed on a reserved number — because MAIN'S TOP TELLS YOU WHAT HAS LANDED, NOT WHAT HAS BEEN RESERVED. Reservations live in the allocator on the canonical box, not in the tree. scripts/decision-block-request.sh anticipates the reasoning exactly: "A campaign that cannot reach the allocator must NOT fall back to picking a number locally — that is precisely the behaviour blocks exist to remove." Re-deriving from a fresh main is that fallback in better clothes, and doing it carefully makes you MORE confident in a wrong answer rather than less.

So the rule, stated for whoever reads this next: THE ALLOCATOR IS THE ONLY AUTHORITY ON DECISION NUMBERS. Not main's top, not a grep of docs/decisions/, not the absence of a conflict. Take a block; it is one command.
